name: Can I change dark oak cabinets to smooth white without replacing them?

mainEntity.name: Can I change dark oak cabinets to smooth white without replacing them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Changing from a dark stain to a light painted color is often possible, but it generally requires more preparation than repainting a similar color. Context: Existing stain, clear coats, oils, grain, and tannins can affect adhesion and color uniformity. The cabinet material and desired sheen determine whether additional primer, sealing, or grain work is needed. Key factors: - Open-grain wood may remain textured unless the grain is filled. - Dark residue can bleed through light finishes without appropriate preparation. - Decorative profiles and routed edges require careful handwork. Practical guidance: Ask for a sample on an actual door, not only a board. Confirm whether the proposal includes stripping, stain blocking, grain filling, and extra coats where needed. Elite Remodeling & Design can coordinate the color change with other kitchen finishes so the new palette works as a complete design.
acceptedAnswer.description: Often, yes, if the doors and boxes are sound, but dark-to-light changes require thorough cleaning, preparation, and products that prevent bleed-through. Open grain may remain visible unless it is filled. Approve a sample on an actual cabinet door first.
